draft.title: Chronic cardiovascular adaptations
card: A chronic adaptation is a lasting change in the body after weeks or months of regular training. It is different from the short-term changes that happen during one session.
Aerobic training makes the heart bigger and stronger, mainly the left ventricle. This is called cardiac hypertrophy.
A stronger left ventricle can fill with more blood and push out more blood with each beat. Stroke volume is the amount of blood pumped out by the heart in one beat, so it rises.
Each beat now moves more blood, so the heart needs fewer beats to deliver the blood the body needs at rest. Resting heart rate falls. Cardiac output is heart rate × stroke volume.
draft.remember: A bigger, stronger heart pumps more blood per beat, so it needs fewer beats at rest.

a.q: After six months of distance running, Tom's resting heart rate has dropped from 70 to 58 beats per minute. What best explains this?
opts: His heart pumps more blood with each beat
His heart now pumps less blood each minute at rest
His heart muscle has become smaller and more efficient
His body now needs less blood to stay alive at rest
a.why: Training raises stroke volume, so the heart can meet the body's needs at rest with fewer beats. The tempting option about less blood each minute is wrong: the body's resting needs are much the same, so the heart still delivers that blood using fewer beats.
a.clue: Think about how much blood each single beat moves.

b.q: Priya's resting cardiac output is the same before and after a year of swim training, but her resting heart rate is now lower. Which change must have happened?
opts: Her stroke volume at rest has risen
Her stroke volume at rest has fallen
Her left ventricle has become weaker
Her body's resting need for blood has fallen
b.why: Cardiac output is heart rate × stroke volume. If output stays the same while heart rate falls, stroke volume must have risen. A weaker ventricle would pump less per beat, so it would not keep output the same with fewer beats.
b.clue: If one part of a product falls and the total stays the same, what must the other part do?

a.best: His heart pumps more blood with each beat

b.best: Her stroke volume at rest has risen

problems.detail: 'A stronger left ventricle can fill with more blood' credits filling to strength. Greater filling comes from the larger chamber volume, while the stronger wall ejects more blood. Saying 'a bigger, stronger left ventricle' would be clearer.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are sound, with one right answer each. One minor wording issue: the card ties the extra filling of the left ventricle to strength rather than to its larger size.
